input.question: How do TV shows maintain their "style" when they seem to switch directors with every episode?
input.ground_truth: I'll use Supernatural as an example. The scripts for the entire season are already written, as that is the main step in pre-production. Depending on how the show is setup, there may be one director contracted to direct X amount of episodes, and the rest is really up to the Executive Producer/Showrunner. [This](_URL_0_) page breaks down every Supernatural episode and who directed it, and almost every single episode this season has been directed by a different person. So each director simply follows the script and is able to give their own stylistic variation, even if you don't see it. If you're adept in the TV world, you notice subtle changes.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do TV shows maintain their "style" when they seem to switch directors with every episode?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of LEGO bricks, and every day you build a different spaceship, but you always use the same colors and the same kind of bricks. Even if your friend helps you build one day and your mom helps you another day, your spaceships all look like they belong together because they use the same colors and shapes.

TV shows are a little like that. They have a special rulebook (called a "style guide") that tells everyone what colors to use, what the rooms look like, how the music sounds, and how the characters act. Even if a different person helps make each episode (like a different friend building your LEGO spaceship), they all look at the rulebook and try to make the show look and sound the same. That way, even if someone new is in charge, the show still feels like the same show you love!
